title: The Princes Who Vanished in the Tower
hook: In 1483, two young princes entered the Tower of London and vanished.
full_narration: In 1483, two young princes entered the Tower of London and vanished. The Tower was a royal fortress beside the River Thames in London. [[pause:0.4]] Twelve-year-old Edward V had come to be crowned king of England. His nine-year-old brother Richard joined him under their uncle’s protection. [[voice:tense]] Their uncle, Richard Duke of Gloucester, controlled the boys and the government. Then he claimed their parents’ marriage was invalid, making the princes illegitimate. [[pause:0.6]] Days later, he took the crown as King Richard the Third. If the boys were legitimate, Richard’s new crown could never feel safe. Then the princes were seen less often, until no one saw them again. [[voice:low]] Two years later, Richard died in battle, but the mystery survived him. The Tower kept its secret, and England still asks what happened to the boys. [[pause:0.8]] Follow for more dark history.

youtube_description: In 1483, two young princes were placed inside the Tower of London and never seen again. Edward V was supposed to become king, but his uncle, Richard Duke of Gloucester, took control of the boys and the government. After declaring them illegitimate, he claimed the crown as Richard III. The princes faded from public view, leaving behind one of England’s most chilling royal mysteries. Their disappearance haunted Richard’s reign, survived his death in battle, and still has no certain answer centuries later.
